text: The reference is the standard hydrogen electrode. A platinum foil, coated with finely divided platinum black, dips into a one molar solution of hydrogen ions at two ninety eight kelvin, while pure hydrogen gas at one bar bubbles over it. The platinum does not react. It only provides a surface for electrons to change hands.
